concepts.name: The rules of a letter sum
concepts.description: Each letter stands for one digit, different letters for different digits, the same letter for the same digit everywhere, and no number of two or more digits starts with 0.

concepts.name: Carries and the leading 1
concepts.description: When two numbers are added, a column passes on a carry of 0 or 1. If the answer has one more digit than both numbers, its first digit is that final carry, so it is 1.

concepts.name: Column-by-column deduction
concepts.description: Work from the units column leftwards: top digits + carry in = digit written + 10 × carry out. Patterns such as A + A ending in A (so A = 0) fix letters quickly; the same working counts how many solutions a puzzle has.

concepts.name: Solving letter sums
concepts.description: Fix the leading 1, then use the columns with the fewest unknowns, trying only the cases a carry allows, until every letter is found. Check the whole sum at the end.

concepts.name: Multiplication cryptarithms
concepts.description: In AB × C = DEB the units digit of the product comes from the units digits alone, and the number of digits limits the size. Facts such as A × A ending in A (A = 0, 1, 5 or 6) cut the cases.

concepts.name: Letter differences
concepts.description: A − B = C is the same puzzle as B + C = A. Rewrite a difference as a sum and use the carry rules on it.

concepts.name: Sums of three words
concepts.description: With three numbers a column can carry 0, 1 or 2 (at most 9 + 9 + 9 + 2 = 29). A + A + A = 3 × A, so a tripled word is a multiplication by 3.

formulas.title: Rules of a cryptarithm
formulas.prompt: What three rules does every letter sum follow?
formulas.formula:
Different letters → different digits
Same letter → same digit everywhere
A number of 2 or more digits never starts with 0
formulas.explanation: The rules are what make the puzzle solvable: without them, any sum of the right length would do.
formulas.example: In BAT + BAT = TALA, A appears three times, so all three places hold the same digit (2 in 621 + 621 = 1242).
formulas.commonMistake: Using one digit for two different letters because the arithmetic works.
formulas.applicationPrompt: In DAL + DAL = RAGA, can D be 0?

formulas.title: Carry in a column
formulas.prompt: When two numbers are added, what carries can a column produce, and what does an extra leading letter equal?
formulas.formula:
Two numbers: carry = 0 or 1 (9 + 9 + 1 = 19)
Answer one digit longer ⇒ its first digit = 1
formulas.explanation: The biggest a column can reach is 9 + 9 + 1 = 19, so the carry is at most 1. A new leading digit is only that last carry.
formulas.example: KITE + KITE = TIGER: two 4-digit numbers give a 5-digit answer, so T = 1.
formulas.commonMistake: Letting the leading letter be 2 because it "looks free".
formulas.applicationPrompt: In TEA + TEA = ROOT, what is R?

formulas.title: The leading 1 at once
formulas.prompt: Two n-digit numbers add to an (n + 1)-digit number. What is the first digit of the answer, without any working?
formulas.explanation: Two numbers below 10ⁿ add to less than 2 × 10ⁿ, so the answer is between 10ⁿ and 2 × 10ⁿ − 2. It starts with 1.
formulas.commonMistake: Applying it when the answer has the same number of digits as the longer word.
formulas.applicationPrompt: In RAKHI + RAKHI = BIHAR, what is B?

formulas.title: The column equation
formulas.prompt: Write the equation every column of a sum obeys.
formulas.formula: top digits + carry in = digit written + 10 × carry out
formulas.explanation: Every column is an ordinary addition. Writing it as an equation shows which letters it links and what carries it allows.
formulas.example: DAL + DAL = BALL, units column: L + L = L + 10 × carry, so L = 0 and the carry is 0.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting the carry coming in from the column to the right.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Write the tens column of BAT + BAT = TALA as an equation.

formulas.title: A letter that reappears below itself
formulas.prompt: In one column of a two-word sum, A + B gives A again. What can B be?
formulas.formula:
A + B ends in A ⇒ B = 0 (carry in 0) or B = 9 (carry in 1)
A + A ends in A ⇒ A = 0 (carry in 0)
formulas.explanation: Adding B left A unchanged in that column, so B + carry is 0 or 10.
formulas.example: DAL + DAL = BALL: L + L ends in L in the units column (no carry in), so L = 0.
formulas.commonMistake: Ruling out 9 by forgetting that a carry of 1 can come in.
formulas.applicationPrompt: In a sum, the tens column reads E + R = E with a carry in of 1. What is R?

formulas.title: Order of attack
formulas.prompt: In what order should you work a letter sum?
formulas.formula:
1. Leading 1 (if the answer is longer)
2. Columns with a repeated letter
3. Units column, then leftwards with carries
4. Check the whole sum
formulas.explanation: Start where the rules give a value outright, then where letters repeat. Each fixed letter shrinks the choices for the rest.
formulas.example: TEA + TEAM = MATH: units A + M ends in H; the thousands column T + carry = M, so M = T + 1; trying T = 6 gives 651 + 6517 = 7168.
formulas.commonMistake: Guessing digits from the left without tracking the carries.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Which letter of IDLI + IDLI = VADA would you look at first?

formulas.title: Units digit of a product
formulas.prompt: Which digits decide the units digit of a product?
formulas.formula:
units(P × Q) = units(units of P × units of Q)
2-digit × 1-digit = 2 or 3 digits
formulas.explanation: Only the units digits reach the units column of a product, and the size of the factors limits how many digits the answer has.
formulas.example: AB × B = ACA: B × B ends in A, and the product has 3 digits; 19 × 9 = 171 fits.
formulas.commonMistake: Using the tens digit to find the units digit of a product.
formulas.applicationPrompt: In AB × C = BBB, what does C × B end in?

formulas.title: Digits that end their own square
formulas.prompt: Which digits A make A × A end in A?
formulas.formula: A × A ends in A ⇒ A = 0, 1, 5 or 6
formulas.explanation: 0² = 0, 1² = 1, 5² = 25, 6² = 36: only these four keep their own last digit.
formulas.example: If a product reads …B × B = …B, then B is 0, 1, 5 or 6; as a multiplier B = 0 or 1 is useless, so B = 5 or 6.
formulas.applicationPrompt: In AB × B = CDB, which values can B take?

formulas.title: A difference as a sum
formulas.prompt: How do you turn a letter difference into a letter sum?
formulas.formula: A − B = C ⇔ B + C = A
formulas.explanation: Adding back what was taken away rebuilds the top number, so all the carry rules for sums apply.
formulas.example: CURD − DAL = CAR is CAR + DAL = CURD, so C = 1 (124 + 925 = 1049).
formulas.commonMistake: Borrowing column by column in the difference and losing track of borrows.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Rewrite READ − TEA = TREE as a sum.

formulas.title: Carries with three numbers
formulas.prompt: What carries can a column of three added numbers produce?
formulas.formula:
Three numbers: carry = 0, 1 or 2 (9 + 9 + 9 + 2 = 29)
A + A + A = 3 × A
formulas.explanation: A column of three digits plus a carry is at most 29, so the carry is at most 2. A word added three times is that word times 3.
formulas.example: GOA + GOA + GOA = SONG: units 3 × A ends in G with a carry of 2 when A = 9 (719 × 3 = 2157).
formulas.commonMistake: Assuming the carry is always 0 or 1, as with two numbers.
formulas.applicationPrompt: In TEA + TEA + TEA = EAR, what is the largest carry the units column could pass on?

levels.title: Letters That Hide Digits
levels.description: The three rules, the leading 1 and working a letter sum column by column with its carries.

blocks.title: Three rules
blocks.body: In a cryptarithm such as DAL + DAL = BALL, each letter stands for a digit. Different letters are different digits, the same letter is the same digit wherever it appears, and a number of two or more digits never starts with 0. A correct sum that breaks a rule is not a solution.

blocks.title: The carry is small, so the leading letter is 1
blocks.body:
Adding two digits and a carry gives at most 9 + 9 + 1 = 19, so a column of a two-number sum passes on a carry of 0 or 1. When the answer has one more digit than both numbers, that extra digit is the last carry: it is 1.

In KITE + KITE = TIGER, two 4-digit numbers add to less than 20,000, so T = 1 before anything else is known.

blocks.title: Every column is an equation
blocks.body: top digits + carry in = digit written + 10 × carry out
blocks.caption: DAL + DAL = BALL: the units column L + L writes L again, so L = 0. Then the tens column A + A writes L = 0, so A = 5 and the carry is 1.

blocks.body: Work from the units column leftwards and write the carry above each column. Start with the leading 1 and with any column where a letter repeats: those fix digits outright.

levels.title: Cryptarithm Rules and Shortcuts
levels.description: The rules, carries, the column equation, units digits of products and differences as sums.

levels.title: First Letter Sums
levels.description: The rules, the leading 1, one column at a time and a first full puzzle.

levels.title: Solving and Counting
levels.description: Full letter sums, how many solutions a puzzle has, carries and a first product.

levels.title: Longer Puzzles and Products
levels.description: Five-letter words, matching letters to digits, the order of a solution and repeated-digit products.

levels.title: Advanced: Differences and Three-Word Sums
levels.description: Turn a letter difference into a sum, and handle carries of 2 when three words are added.

blocks.title: A difference is a sum in disguise
blocks.body: A − B = C says exactly the same as B + C = A. Rewrite CURD − DAL = CAR as CAR + DAL = CURD, and every sum rule applies: the answer is one digit longer, so C = 1. Borrowing never has to be tracked.

blocks.title: Three numbers carry up to 2
blocks.caption: With two numbers the carry is 0 or 1; with three it can be 2. The answer can also start with 1 or 2.

blocks.title: A word added three times
blocks.body: TEA + TEA + TEA = 3 × TEA. If the answer EAR still has three digits, TEA is at most 333, so T is 1, 2 or 3. Then each column reads 3 × digit + carry.
In GOA + GOA + GOA = SONG the units column is 9 + 9 + 9 = 27: it writes 7 and carries 2. Assuming the carry is 1 makes this puzzle look impossible.

levels.title: Challenge: Differences, Triples and Counts
levels.description: Letter differences, three-word sums and counting the solutions of a puzzle, against the clock.

questions.question: In a letter sum, two different letters, say K and T, may both stand for 7 if that makes the addition come out right.
questions.explanation: The rules say different letters stand for different digits. If K and T were both 7, the puzzle would not be solved, however well the arithmetic works.
questions.method: Check the three rules before the arithmetic.

hints.text: How many digits can one letter stand for, and can two letters share one?
Read the first rule on the formula card: different letters, different digits.

commonMistakes: Accepting any assignment that makes the sum correct.

questions.question: KITE + KITE = TIGER, where each letter stands for a different digit. Without solving the rest, what digit is T?
questions.explanation: Two 4-digit numbers add to less than 2 × 10,000 = 20,000, so a 5-digit answer must start with 1. T = 1. (The full solution is 7512 + 7512 = 15024.)
solutionSteps: TIGER has 5 digits, so it is between 10,000 and 19,998.
questions.method: An extra leading digit is the final carry, which is 1.

hints.text: How big can the sum of two 4-digit numbers be?
Below 20,000, so what must a 5-digit answer start with?

commonMistakes: Answering 2 because K + K looks like it doubles.
Answering 0: a number cannot start with 0.

questions.question: DAL + DAL = BALL, where each letter stands for a different digit. Look only at the units column. What is L?
questions.explanation: The units column reads L + L = L (with a carry out). So L + L − L = L must be 0 or 10; L = 0 gives 0 + 0 = 0 with no carry. L = 5 gives 5 + 5 = 10, which writes 0, not 5. The puzzle solves as 750 + 750 = 1500.
solutionSteps: Units: L + L ends in L.
So L itself ends in 0: L = 0.
questions.method: A letter that reappears under itself after adding forces the other addend to be 0.

hints.text: Write the units column: L + L = ? and the digit written is L.
Which digit doubled ends in itself?

commonMistakes: Choosing 5 because 5 + 5 = 10 "ends nicely": it writes 0, not 5.

questions.question: In a multiplication puzzle, A × A ends in the digit A. Which set holds every possible value of A?
questions.explanation: 0 × 0 = 0, 1 × 1 = 1, 5 × 5 = 25 and 6 × 6 = 36 all end in the digit squared. 4 × 4 = 16 and 9 × 9 = 81 do not, and nor does any other digit.
questions.method: Check the units digit of each square.

hints.text: List the last digits of 0², 1², …, 9².
Which of those equal the digit you started with?

commonMistakes: Leaving out 0 or 6.
Including 4 or 9, whose squares end in 6 and 1.

questions.question: DAL + DAL = RAGA, where each letter stands for a different digit and no number starts with 0. What number is RAGA?
questions.explanation: R = 1 (two 3-digit numbers make a 4-digit one). Hundreds: D + D + carry = 1A, and tens A + A + carry gives G while units L + L gives A. Trying A even from the units column, A = 4 with L = 2 gives tens 4 + 4 = 8 = G and hundreds 7 + 7 = 14, so D = 7: 742 + 742 = 1484.
solutionSteps: Units: L + L = A (A is even).
questions.method: Leading 1 first, then pair the units and hundreds columns, which share A.

hints.text: R is the extra leading digit. What must it be?
A appears in the units of the answer and in its hundreds place: units L + L = A, hundreds D + D + carry = 1A.

commonMistakes: Giving the value of DAL (742) instead of RAGA.

questions.question: IDLI + IDLI = VADA, where each letter stands for a different digit and no number starts with 0. What number is VADA?
questions.explanation: A appears in the tens and the units of VADA. Units: I + I = A; tens: L + L + carry = D. Hundreds: D + D + carry = A, and thousands I + I + carry = V, a single digit, so I ≤ 4. Trying I = 3 gives A = 6, then D = 8 from 2D + carry = 16 (carry 0, D = 8), L = 4 from 2L = 8: 3843 + 3843 = 7686, V = 7.
questions.method: Bound the leading letter, then link the columns that share a letter.

hints.text: VADA has only 4 digits. What does that say about I?
Units: I + I = A. Hundreds: D + D (+ carry) must end in the same A.

commonMistakes: Assuming V = 1: VADA is not longer than IDLI, so there is no leading 1.

questions.question: How many solutions does AB + AB = CA have? Each letter is a different digit, and AB and CA are two-digit numbers (so A and C are not 0).
questions.explanation: AB + AB = 2 × AB must be the two-digit number CA, so AB ≤ 49 and the units digit of 2B is A, so A is even: A = 2 or 4. A = 2: B = 1 (21 + 21 = 42) or B = 6 (26 + 26 = 52). A = 4: B = 2 (42 + 42 = 84) or B = 7 (47 + 47 = 94). Each has distinct digits, so there are 4 solutions.
solutionSteps: Units of 2B is A, so A is even: 2 or 4.
questions.method: Use the units column to list the cases, then check each one.

hints.text: 2 × AB is still a two-digit number. How big can A be?
The units digit of B + B is A, so A is even. Try A = 2 and A = 4.

commonMistakes: Stopping at the first solution.
Forgetting B can give a carry: B = 6 and B = 7 work too.

questions.question: HOLI + HOLI = LION has exactly one solution. In it, the hundreds column passes a carry of 1 to the thousands column.
questions.explanation: The solution is 1632 + 1632 = 3264 (H = 1, O = 6, L = 3, I = 2, N = 4). Hundreds column: O + O = 6 + 6 = 12, so it writes 2 (I) and carries 1. The thousands column then reads 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 = L.
questions.method: Find the solution, then read the carry column by column.

hints.text: LION has only 4 digits, so H is small. Start from H + H + carry = L.
Units: I + I = N. The hundreds column O + O must end in I.

commonMistakes: Reading the carry out of the tens column instead of the hundreds column.

questions.question: AB × B = ACA, where each letter is a different digit and AB and ACA do not start with 0. What is the two-digit number AB?
questions.explanation: The product starts and ends with A. B × B ends in A. If A = 1, B × B ends in 1, so B = 9 (B = 1 would equal A): 19 × 9 = 171, and C = 7 fits. A larger A fails: A = 4 needs B = 2 or 8, but 42 × 2 = 84 has 2 digits and 48 × 8 = 384 does not start with 4; A = 6 needs B = 4 or 6 (64 × 4 = 256, no); A = 9 needs B = 3 or 7 (93 × 3 = 279, 97 × 7 = 679, no).
solutionSteps: Try A = 1: B = 9 → 19 × 9 = 171 = ACA with C = 7.
Other A values fail the first digit.
questions.method: Units digits first, then check the size of the product.

hints.text: The units digit of B × B is A.
ACA has 3 digits but AB × B must start with the same A. Try a small A.

commonMistakes: Answering the product 171.
Trying B = 1 with A = 1: two letters cannot share a digit.

questions.question: TEA + TEAM = MATH, where each letter is a different digit and no number starts with 0. What is M?
questions.explanation: MATH has the same number of digits as TEAM, so M is not forced to be 1. The thousands column reads T + carry = M, so M = T + 1. Working the columns gives T = 6, E = 5, A = 1, H = 8 and M = 7: 651 + 6517 = 7168.
solutionSteps: Thousands: T + carry = M, so M = T + 1.
questions.method: Read the leftmost column first: it ties M to T.

hints.text: Is MATH longer than TEAM? If not, the leading-1 rule does not apply.
Thousands column: T + carry = M. Units: A + M ends in H.

commonMistakes: Assuming M = 1 by the leading-1 rule, which needs a longer answer.
Giving T (6) instead of M.

questions.question: For SIX + SIX = HILL, Kabir offers 672 + 672 = 1344. The addition is correct. Which rule of cryptarithms does his answer break?

options.text: The same letter, I, stands for two different digits
Two different letters stand for the same digit

questions.explanation: Reading SIX = 672 gives I = 7, but reading HILL = 1344 gives I = 3. One letter must keep one digit. (No two letters share a digit here, and nothing starts with 0.) The real solution is 872 + 872 = 1744.
solutionSteps: I is both 7 and 3: the same letter has two digits.
questions.method: Match each letter with its digit in every place it appears.

hints.text: Write each letter under its digit in both numbers.
Look at I: what is it in SIX, and what in HILL?

commonMistakes: Accepting it because 672 + 672 = 1344 is correct arithmetic.

questions.question: TABLA + TABLA = BANYAN, where each letter is a different digit and no number starts with 0. What number is TABLA?
questions.explanation: B = 1 (5-digit + 5-digit = 6-digit). Units: A + A ends in N; tens: L + L + carry ends in A; ten-thousands: T + T + carry = 1A. Since 2T + carry ≥ 10 + A, T is large. Trying the cases with the carries gives T = 8, A = 7, L = 3, N = 4, Y = 2: 87137 + 87137 = 174274.
solutionSteps: Hundreds: B + B + carry = 2 or 3 ends in Y.
questions.method: Leading 1, then the column B + B, then link the columns that share A.

hints.text: BANYAN is one digit longer. What is B? Then the hundreds column B + B + carry gives Y directly.
A sits in the units of TABLA and the tens and ten-thousands places of BANYAN: units A + A gives N, tens L + L + carry gives A.

commonMistakes: Giving BANYAN (174274) instead of TABLA.

questions.question: SITAR + STAR = TRAIN has exactly one solution. Match each letter with its digit.
questions.explanation: The solution is 38491 + 3491 = 41982: S = 3, I = 8, T = 4, A = 9, R = 1, N = 2. TRAIN is not longer than SITAR, so T is not forced to be 1; the ten-thousands column gives T = S + 1 (with a carry of 1 from the thousands column).
solutionSteps: Units: R + R = N; tens: A + A + carry ends in I.
questions.method: Work the columns right to left, keeping track of every carry.

hints.text: SITAR has a ten-thousands digit and STAR does not, so T = S + carry.
Units R + R = N with N even; thousands I + S + carry ends in R.

commonMistakes: Setting T = 1 by the leading-1 rule; the answer is not longer than SITAR.

questions.question: Put the steps in order to solve BAT + BAT = TALA.

steps.text: TALA is one digit longer than BAT, so T = 1
Units column: T + T = 1 + 1 = 2, so A = 2 with no carry
Tens column: A + A = 2 + 2 = 4, so L = 4 with no carry
Hundreds column: B + B = 12 (writing A = 2, carrying T = 1), so B = 6

questions.explanation: The leading 1 comes first because it needs no other letter. Then each column from the right uses only letters already found and the carry from the column before it.
questions.method: Leading 1, then right to left.

hints.text: Which letter can be found without knowing any other?
After T, work from the units column leftwards.

commonMistakes: Starting at the hundreds column before A is known.

questions.question: GOAL + GOAL = AGRA has exactly one solution. Select ALL the statements that are true of it.
questions.explanation: The solution is 2147 + 2147 = 4294: G = 2, O = 1, A = 4, L = 7, R = 9. A is the units digit of L + L, so it is even. AGRA has 4 digits, so the thousands column G + G + carry = A has no carry out; here A = 4 = 2 × 2. L = 7 is not less than 5 (it makes the units carry 1). R = 9 is odd.
questions.method: Solve it, then test each statement.

hints.text: A is written in the units of AGRA, under L + L. What does that say about A?
Thousands: G + G + carry = A with no carry out. Try G = 2.

commonMistakes: Ticking "L is less than 5" without checking the carry into the tens column.

questions.question: AB × C = BBB, where each letter is a different digit and AB does not start with 0. What is AB?
questions.explanation: BBB = B × 111 = B × 3 × 37, so AB × C is a multiple of 37: AB = 37 or 74 (two-digit multiples). AB = 37 needs B = 7, but 37 × C = 777 gives C = 21, not a digit. AB = 74 needs B = 4: 74 × C = 444 gives C = 6. So AB = 74, C = 6.
questions.method: Factor the repeated-digit product: BBB = 111 × B.

hints.text: A number with three equal digits is a multiple of 111 = 3 × 37.
Which two-digit multiples of 37 end in the digit their product repeats?

commonMistakes: Choosing 37 because 37 × 3 = 111, which needs B = 1 and B = 7 at once.

questions.question: CURD − DAL = CAR, where each letter is a different digit and no number starts with 0. What number is CURD?
questions.explanation: Rewrite it as CAR + DAL = CURD. Two 3-digit numbers make a 4-digit one, so C = 1. Hundreds: 1 + D + carry = 10 + U, with U ≠ 1, so U = 0 and D = 9 (no carry) or D = 8 (carry 1). Working the units R + L = D and tens A + A + carry = R gives 124 + 925 = 1049. So CURD = 1049.
solutionSteps: CURD − DAL = CAR ⇔ CAR + DAL = CURD.
questions.method: Turn the difference into a sum, then use the leading 1.

hints.text: A − B = C is the same as B + C = A. Rewrite it.
CAR + DAL = CURD: the answer is one digit longer, so C = 1.

commonMistakes: Borrowing column by column and losing a borrow.
Giving CAR (124) instead of CURD.

questions.question: TEA + TEA + TEA = EAR, where each letter is a different digit and no number starts with 0. What number is TEA?
questions.explanation: TEA + TEA + TEA = 3 × TEA, and EAR still has 3 digits, so TEA ≤ 333 and T is 1, 2 or 3. Hundreds: 3T + carry = E. Units: 3A ends in R; tens: 3E + carry ends in A. T = 1, E = 4, A = 2, R = 6 fits: 3 × 142 = 426.
solutionSteps: T = 1, E = 4: tens 12 + carry ends in A = 2; units 3 × 2 = 6 = R.
questions.method: Treat a word added three times as the word times 3.

hints.text: TEA + TEA + TEA = 3 × TEA. How large can TEA be if EAR has 3 digits?
Hundreds: 3 × T + carry = E. Try T = 1.

commonMistakes: Giving EAR (426) instead of TEA.

questions.question: READ − TEA = TREE, where each letter is a different digit and no number starts with 0. What is R?
questions.explanation: As a sum: TEA + TREE = READ. READ has the same number of digits as TREE, so R is not forced to be 1. The thousands column gives R = T + carry. Solving gives T = 5, E = 1, A = 2, D = 3 and R = 6: 512 + 5611 = 6123, so 6123 − 512 = 5611.
solutionSteps: READ − TEA = TREE ⇔ TEA + TREE = READ.
questions.method: Rewrite as a sum and read the leftmost column.

hints.text: Rewrite as TEA + TREE = READ.
Units: A + E = D; tens: E + E + carry ends in A. The thousands column links R and T.

commonMistakes: Answering 1 by the leading-1 rule; READ is not longer than TREE.
Answering 5, the value of T.

questions.question: GOA + GOA + GOA = SONG has exactly one solution. In it, what carry does the units column pass to the tens column?
questions.explanation: The solution is 719 + 719 + 719 = 2157 (G = 7, O = 1, A = 9, S = 2, N = 5). Units: 9 + 9 + 9 = 27, so it writes 7 (G) and carries 2. With three numbers a carry of 2 is possible, unlike with two.
questions.method: Find the solution, then read the units column.

hints.text: Units: A + A + A ends in G; tens: O + O + O + carry ends in N.
SONG has 4 digits, so 3 × GOA ≥ 1000. Try G = 7.

commonMistakes: Assuming a carry can only be 0 or 1.

questions.question: When three numbers are added, a column can pass a carry of 2 to the next column, but never a carry of 3.
questions.explanation: The largest a column can reach is 9 + 9 + 9 plus the largest carry in. If carries are at most 2, that is 27 + 2 = 29, which carries 2. So a carry of 3 never happens, starting from the units column (27, carry 2).
solutionSteps: Any later column: at most 27 + 2 = 29 → carry ≤ 2.
questions.method: Find the largest possible column total.

hints.text: What is the largest total in the units column of three numbers?
Add the largest carry to 9 + 9 + 9 for the next column.

commonMistakes: Thinking the carry can grow column after column.

questions.question: How many solutions does AB + BA = CC have? Each letter is a different digit, and AB, BA and CC are two-digit numbers (so A, B and C are not 0).
questions.explanation: AB + BA = 11 × (A + B) and CC = 11 × C, so A + B = C. Since C is a digit, A + B ≤ 9, with A ≠ B and both at least 1 (C is then different from both automatically). Ordered pairs with A + B = 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9: 2, 2, 4, 4, 6, 6, 8. Total 32.
solutionSteps: So A + B = C ≤ 9, A ≠ B, A, B ≥ 1.
questions.method: Turn the puzzle into one equation in the digits, then count.

hints.text: AB = 10A + B and BA = 10B + A. What is their sum?
The equation becomes A + B = C. Count ordered pairs of different digits from 1 to 9 with a sum of at most 9.

commonMistakes: Counting unordered pairs (16): AB = 12 and AB = 21 are different solutions.
Allowing A = B, such as 22 + 22 = 44.
